speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a fever and altered mental status for two days; to help me understand your condition better, have you experienced any seizures, confusion, or headaches during this time?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

I have noted your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, which can cause rigidity, fever, and altered mental status. Given the specific combination of fever and altered mentation without a clear infectious source or seizure activity, this clinical picture strongly points towards a drug-induced reaction.
